description: Transportation Networks for Research is a GitHub repository of networks for transportation research, mainly test problems for the traffic assignment problem. It continues Hillel Bar-Gera's TNTP collection, with updates made only here since 1 May 2016. It lists 23 networks, from the Braess example and Sioux Falls (24 zones, 76 links) to Anaheim, Austin (18,961 links), Barcelona, several Berlin networks, Birmingham, Chicago Sketch and Chicago regional (39,018 links), Eastern Massachusetts, Gold Coast, Hessen, Philadelphia (40,003 links), Sydney (75,379 links), Terrassa, Winnipeg and a transportation electrification network; each folder holds network and trip table files, mostly in the TNTP format, with a README, and scripts are provided. Coverage is these cities and regions worldwide. Access: free to download from GitHub; all data are donated and for academic research purposes only, and users must cite the source. Caveats: the team is not responsible for content or correctness, one network is not in the TNTP format, and copies elsewhere (such as a Kaggle mirror of Eastern Massachusetts) may drift from the original. It supports benchmarking of traffic assignment, network design and resilience algorithms, and complements the TrainRuns.jl and TransCAD records catalogued here.
